This cancelled typescript concerns morphisms of topoi. It carries the revised section number 3.1.2, its own handwritten page number read as `\unsure{2|7}2`, and an inverted archive 27. The first digit is unresolved: C gave 22 and H described 72. There is no visible title, date, or total page count. Its relationship to the adjacent Kostant papers is not supplied by the page; H's description of reuse is editorial context, not manuscript text.

The opening continuation states uniqueness up to unique isomorphism from the inverse or direct image functor. The section assigns projective limits to the right adjoint `u_*`, inductive limits to its left adjoint `u^*`, and finite projective limits to `u^*` by the extra hypothesis. The addition above the last assertion reads `est ex\unsure{.|a}ct à gauche i.e.`: the small central form is a filled point without a distinguishable bowl, so the point is first despite the mathematically expected word. The baseline `commute aux limites projectives finies` remains locally live, within the overall sheet cancellation; H's claim that the addition replaces that phrase is not supported by a local strike. The two C doubts about the initial digits have different outcomes: the old section digit resolves to 2, while the old digit in the upper reference remains 2|3. The crossed body and margin references each retain two final 1 strokes; their preceding obscured forms remain unresolved. No numerical reference was repaired from an expected theorem.

This run checked uniqueness in the sense of compatibility with the adjunction identifications, using Yoneda; it did not assert the absence of automorphisms after forgetting adjunction data. It also wrote out the Hom/universal-property proof that right adjoints preserve limits and left adjoints preserve colimits. With the stated finite-limit hypothesis, this gives the exactness used here. These are internal proofs; the structural fact that topos epimorphisms are effective was carried as background. R1 independently reported the Hom calculation, R2 rechecked its direction and typing, and R3 checked typing/variance only. Their check events distinguish these activities.

The structure passage discusses data of arrows and constructions by finite projective limits and arbitrary inductive limits. It lists groups, rings, modules, comodules, bialgebras and torsors, preserving `est muni`, singular `celle`, and `comodule sur un anneau`. This run directly transported the finite-product operations and equations for groups, rings and modules. It also checked torsors by the conditions that `P → 1` is epi and `G × P → P × P` is an isomorphism. The general construction principle is conditional on explicitly given finite-limit/colimit data. Complete tensor, coalgebra, comodule and bialgebra data are not specified on this clipped page, and no full independent verification of those examples is claimed. The ordinary E in the parenthesis has additional heavy lower material; a second complete E impression cannot be separated, so C's definite blackboard E is replaced by a definite ordinary E plus an uncertain drawing. The first object's E and both footer U letters have separate underlines. H's script U is rejected on the ordinary typed slab-serif form.

The author's express hesitation is: “Plutôt que d'entrer dans la tâche peu engageante de donner un sens précis à cet énoncé et de le justifier de façon formelle”. The raised insertion `l'expliciter et de` tells the reader to work through the examples and convince himself of validity. This is a source statement that a general formalization is being avoided here, not evidence that such a proof occurs on the sheet. The footnote's `vérifier que` is readable but locally cancelled and replaced by `(1.5 et 1.8)`; it is not a surviving instruction. The final `D'ailleurs` sentence is also locally cancelled, with its opening word, comma and final subdivision still doubtful.

The footnote asserts an adjoint-existence criterion from preservation of the corresponding U-small limits or colimits. This run supplied an internal special-adjoint argument under explicit structural hypotheses: local U-smallness, completeness/cocompleteness, wellpoweredness/cowellpoweredness and a U-small separating family for the Grothendieck topoi. These topos structural facts were background, not derived from sites in this run. A cogenerator was constructed as a product of powers of the subobject classifier, using graphs to separate arrows; no assertion that the coproduct of a separating family is a generator was used. For a limit-preserving functor, the proof constructs a small weakly initial family in the comma category using equalizers, a small family of products of cogenerators and their subobjects, then obtains an initial object by equalizing the endomorphisms of a weakly initial object. The dual gives the colimit-preserving direction. Full details and limitations are in `math_checks/123_028_adjoint_and_structure_checks.md`.
